story.label: Stamped concrete process

stages.title: Press the pattern into fresh concrete
stages.body: Stamp mats are laid on the fresh slab and pressed in, so the surface takes on stone, brick or slate texture.

stages.title: Tamp to an even depth
stages.body: Release powder keeps the mats from sticking while the pattern is tamped in evenly across the surface.

stages.title: Lift the mat to reveal the impression
stages.body: Lifting the mat shows the crisp joints and stone texture left in the surface.

stages.title: Seal the finished surface
stages.body: The finished surface is sealed. Here, a sealed grey herringbone.

items.q: How long does decorative concrete last?
items.a: With a sound sub-base and the right sealer, decorative concrete is a long-lasting surface. Lifespan depends on use, climate and maintenance.
Sweep regularly and wash with a mild cleaner. Avoid harsh acids on sealed surfaces.
Sealers wear with traffic and sun, so exposed outdoor areas are resealed more often than indoor floors.
Any concrete can develop hairline cracks. Control joints guide where movement happens, and a stamped pattern can hide joints in its lines.
Area, finish type, thickness and reinforcement, site access, base condition and sealer all affect the price. A site visit gives the most accurate quote.

items.q: How long will my project take?
items.a: It depends on size, finish and curing time. We confirm the schedule in your quote.
Slip resistance depends on the finish and sealer. Textured stamped finishes and anti-slip sealer additives are options for wet or sloped areas.

items.q: Can you pour in Jordan's summer heat?
items.a: Hot weather affects setting and curing. Pours are planned for cooler hours and the surface is protected while it cures.

about.title: About us
about.intro: We're The Concrete Factory, based in Amman and working across Jordan. For more than 10 years we've helped people get concrete right, from a family courtyard to a factory floor.
about.storyP1: After more than 10 years, we've learned that a good floor is mostly decided before any concrete is poured. The loads, the traffic, the joints, the reinforcement and the finish all work together, so we like to sit down with you early and get them right.
about.storyP2: We work with every type of reinforcement and we help you choose the finish, whether that's stamped, polished, epoxy or polyurethane, and we partner with the best global suppliers for the materials we recommend. In the industrial floor market in Jordan, we're leaders, and we bring that experience to every home too.
about.storyP3: Whether it's a courtyard, a kitchen island or a warehouse slab, you'll get honest advice, a clear plan and people who care how it turns out.

principles.d: We help you decide the details before the pour, when it's easiest and cheapest to get them right.
We'll tell you what you need and what you don't.
More than 10 years of work across floors, walls and built-ins.
We work with the best global suppliers for the materials we recommend.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.draftNote: This policy describes how the website works today. It should be reviewed by your legal adviser before launch.

sections.p: This website is operated by The Concrete Factory, based in Amman, Jordan. You can reach us at {email}.

When you send a quote request, book a sample visit or request a sample box, we receive what you type: your name, mobile number, email address (if you give it), project details, the finishes you chose and any photos or drawings you attach.
We use your details only to reply to your request, prepare a quote, arrange a visit or send samples. We do not sell your details.

Requests are delivered to us by email through our email provider, Resend. The website is hosted by Vercel. If you continue a request on WhatsApp, WhatsApp's own privacy policy applies to that conversation.

We do not use advertising or tracking cookies. Your browser stores your sample list and an unfinished quote draft on your own device so you can come back to them. You can clear them at any time in your browser settings.
We keep requests for as long as we need them to deal with your project and our records.
You can ask us what we hold about you, ask us to correct it or ask us to delete it by emailing {email}.
